DecisionDomain.description:
The distinct legal authorities this system analyses against.

ADR-003 and blueprint §2.1: suitability, fitness, PIV credentialing, and national-security
eligibility are distinct authorities with distinct criteria. Collapsing them produces
analysis that is wrong in a way that is hard to detect, so every finding names exactly one.
DecisionDomain.title: DecisionDomain

FindingAuthority.description:
The single authority and criterion this finding is analysed under.

One authority per finding, always. Blueprint §2.1: collapsing distinct authorities produces
analysis that is wrong in a way that is hard to detect. If the same conduct is relevant under
both 5 CFR 731 and SEAD-4, that is two findings with two criteria, joined at synthesis by
de-duplication that preserves both — not one finding with a merged rationale.

policy_citations.description: At least one. A policy-relevance claim with no resolvable policy citation is exactly what the deterministic validator exists to reject.
policy_citations.title: Policy Citations

FindingAuthority.title: FindingAuthority

FindingClassification.description:
What kind of thing this finding is.

Every member is a statement about the *record*, not about the person. There is deliberately
no member meaning "adverse", "disqualifying", or "cleared" — those are determinations.
FindingClassification.title: FindingClassification

FindingValidation.description:
Results of the deterministic validators (blueprint §8.1, §10.4).

The model does not decide whether its own output is valid — `CLAUDE.md`, "deterministic
shell around probabilistic reasoning". These outcomes are written by validator code.

schema_check.description: Named `schema_check` rather than blueprint §10.4's `schema`, which would shadow a BaseModel attribute. Divergence is cosmetic.

citations.description: Every cited evidence and policy id resolved against the run's snapshots.

FindingValidation.title: FindingValidation

GeneratedBy.description:
Provenance of the machine proposal.

`model_alias` is an alias, never a model ID (ADR-008). Blueprint §10.4's example carries a
concrete model name; this is a deliberate divergence so that a partition or model-generation
change stays a LiteLLM config change.
GeneratedBy.title: GeneratedBy

InformationGap.description:
A question for the reviewer.

Blueprint §8.4: the `propose_information_gap` tool records a question — it does not authorize
external investigation or contact. Nothing in this contract carries an action to take.

blocking.description: True when analysis under this criterion cannot be completed without an answer.
blocking.title: Blocking

InformationGap.title: InformationGap

ModelAlias.description:
The only model references application code and contracts may carry.

ADR-008: concrete Bedrock model IDs, inference-profile IDs, and regions live in LiteLLM
config. A partition change must be a config change, so a model ID must never reach a
contract. Blueprint §10.3's example run manifest names a concrete model
(`case-analysis-sonnet`); that is a divergence this enum deliberately closes.
ModelAlias.title: ModelAlias

ProposedFinding.description:
A machine-proposed finding, pending human disposition.

Immutable by construction (`ContractModel` is frozen). ADR-011 requires that both the machine
proposal and the human-approved version are retained, which only works if the proposal cannot
be edited in place.

observation.description: What the record indicates. Descriptive, and fully supported by cited evidence.
observation.title: Observation

policy_relevance.description: Why this may be relevant under the cited criterion. 'May be relevant' is the ceiling — relevance is proposed, applicability is the officer's call.
policy_relevance.title: Policy Relevance

mitigating_factors.description: Whole-person and mitigation analysis is required, not optional (blueprint §8.3.6). A finding that records only aggravating factors is a red flag in evaluation.
mitigating_factors.title: Mitigating Factors

evidence_confidence.description: How solid the underlying record is — source reliability and corroboration.

analysis_confidence.description: How confident the analysis is that the criterion is implicated at all.

recommended_officer_action.description: What the officer should *review*, never what they should decide. 'Review the cited records and resolve the gaps' is in bounds; any recommended adjudicative outcome is rejected by the language guard.
recommended_officer_action.title: Recommended Officer Action

ProposedFinding.title: ProposedFinding

ReviewUrgency.description:
Sequencing hint for the reviewer's queue.

This is not a severity score and must not become one. It says how soon a human should look,
not how serious the underlying conduct is — the latter is an adjudicative judgment. It is
per-finding and is never aggregated across findings or across a person (ADR-014).
ReviewUrgency.title: ReviewUrgency

SpecialistCriterion.description:
The criterion a specialist sub-call was pointed at.

A sibling to the per-finding authority type used elsewhere in this package — it shares the
same four identifying fields (`decision_domain`, `policy_pack_id`, `policy_id`,
`criterion_id`) but deliberately omits that type's fifth field, the list of policy citation
ids required to have at least one entry (D-04). A query does not cite; a finding does. Policy
citations belong to the proposed findings this criterion produces, not to the act of asking
the question. Not a subclass of that type, and it is not imported here.
SpecialistCriterion.title: SpecialistCriterion

description:
The return value of one specialist sub-agent call.

Required, not `Optional` (D-05): `criterion` is populated even when `findings` is empty, so a
result with zero findings still says what was checked. This is the whole reason the wrapper
exists rather than returning a bare `list[ProposedFinding]`.
title: SpecialistResult
